questions.text:
Consider the set X={a, b,c,d,e} under the partial ordering R={(a,a),(a,b),(a,c),(a,d),(a,e),(b,b),(b,c),(b,e),(c,c),(c,e),(d,d),(d,e),(e,e)}.
The Hasse diagram of the partial order (X, R) is shown below.

The minimum number of ordered pairs that need to be added to R to make (X, R) a lattice is _____.
questions.solution:
Check the Hasse diagram: a is the bottom, e is the top, with chains a [latex]\lt[/latex] b [latex]\lt[/latex] c [latex]\lt[/latex] e and a [latex]\lt[/latex] d [latex]\lt[/latex] e. Every pair has a least upper bound and a greatest lower bound (e.g. join(c, d) = e, meet(c, d) = a). So it is already a lattice: 0 pairs needed.

Answer: 0

questions.text: The Breadth First Search (BFS) algorithm has been implemented using the queue data structure. Which one of the following is a possible order of visiting the nodes in the graph below?
questions.solution:
BFS from P: neighbours O, Q; then O's new neighbour N, Q's new neighbour M; then M's new neighbour R [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] P O Q N M R True

The others break BFS order, e.g. MNOPQR visits O before Q and R, which are M's own neighbours.

Answer: POQNMR

questions.text:
Let p, q, r denote the statements "It is raining ," It is cold", and " It is pleasant,"
respectively. Then the statement "It is not raining and it is pleasant, and it is not pleasant
only if it is raining and it is cold" is represented by
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- "It is not raining and it is pleasant": [latex] eg p\wedge r[/latex]
- "It is not pleasant only if it is raining and cold": "A only if B" means [latex]A ightarrow B[/latex], so [latex] eg r ightarrow(p\wedge q)[/latex]

Joined by "and": [latex]( eg p\wedge r)\wedge( eg r ightarrow(p\wedge q))[/latex]

Answer: Option 1

questions.text:
The number of integers between 1 and 500 (both inclusive) that are divisible by 3 or 5 or 7 is
______________.
questions.solution:
Inclusion-exclusion for 1-500:
[latex]\lfloor\tfrac{500}{3}\rfloor+\lfloor\tfrac{500}{5}\rfloor+\lfloor\tfrac{500}{7}\rfloor-\lfloor\tfrac{500}{15}\rfloor-\lfloor\tfrac{500}{21}\rfloor-\lfloor\tfrac{500}{35}\rfloor+\lfloor\tfrac{500}{105}\rfloor[/latex]
= 166 + 100 + 71 [latex]-[/latex] 33 [latex]-[/latex] 23 [latex]-[/latex] 14 + 4 = 271

Answer: 271

questions.text:
Let p, q, and r be propositions and the expression (p[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]q)[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]r be a contradiction. Then, the
expression (r[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]p)[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]q is
questions.solution:
[latex](p\rightarrow q)\rightarrow r[/latex] is always false, so [latex]p\rightarrow q[/latex] is always true and r is always false.

Then [latex]r\rightarrow p[/latex] is true (r is false), so [latex](r\rightarrow p)\rightarrow q\equiv q[/latex]. It is true exactly when q is true.

Answer: always TRUE when q is TRUE
